`head`: output the first part of files.

## Synopsis

<strong>head</strong> \[<strong>-n</strong> <em>lines</em>\] \[<strong>-c</strong> <em>bytes</em>\] \[<em>file</em>...\]

## Description

<strong>head</strong> writes the first 10 lines of each <em>file</em> to standard output. With no <em>file</em>, or where a <em>file</em> is <strong>-</strong>, it reads standard input.

With more than one <em>file</em>, each one's output is preceded by a header, <strong>==\></strong> <em>name</em> <strong>\<==</strong> (<strong>standard input</strong> for <strong>-</strong>), with a blank line between files.

## Options

<strong>-n</strong> <em>lines</em>, <strong>-n</strong><em>lines</em>, <strong>-</strong><em>lines</em>
: Print the first <em>lines</em> lines instead of 10. <strong>-n</strong> also turns off an earlier <strong>-c</strong>.

<strong>-c</strong> <em>bytes</em>, <strong>-c</strong><em>bytes</em>
: Print the first <em>bytes</em> bytes instead of lines.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 if a file could not be opened or a number was invalid.

## Examples

```text
head -n 3 /init.lua
ls -1 | head -5
```

## Notes

Negative counts (GNU's "all but the last <em>n</em>") are not supported.

## See also

<strong>tail</strong>(1), <strong>cat</strong>(1), <strong>less</strong>(1)
